paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: The figure is a nested (two-ring) donut pie chart showing the distribution of samples (in percent) across two ambiguity-related categorizations: the outer ring represents “Ambiguity Std” (standard deviation) and the inner ring represents “Max Ambiguity.” There are 7 slices total across both rings (4 in the outer ring and 3 in the inner ring). In the outer ring (Ambiguity Std), the slices are labeled and colored in progressively lighter blue tones: “Std: 0.0” (dark teal-blue) at approximately 49.0%, “Std: 0.47” (dark blue) at approximately 39.0%, “Std: 0.82” (medium-bright blue) at approximately 5.0%, and “Std: 0.94” (light/bright blue) at approximately 7.0%. In the inner ring (Max Ambiguity), the slices are in lighter cyan-blue tones: “Max: 1” (medium light cyan) at approximately 47.7%, “Max: 2” (light cyan) at approximately 38.0%, and “Max: 3” (very pale blue) at approximately 14.2%. Percentage labels are shown directly on the slices, and two separate legends appear on the right side of the chart (one for the outer ring and one for the inner ring); no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized, and the segments do not appear strictly ordered by size around the circle.
